# Brewer Family Companies

> The Brewer family's history and companies in Bricktown, Oklahoma City. Jim D. Brewer (1937–2008) helped turn Bricktown's warehouses into an entertainment destination; his sons Brent and Brett Brewer carry the family's businesses forward.

## Key facts
- Jim Brewer: Oklahoma City entrepreneur, born February 6, 1937, died November 11, 2008. Worked in transmissions, nightclubs and oil before investing in downtown real estate.
- Bricktown Haunted Warehouse: opened 1986 in the Hunzicker Building, 101 E. California; about 18,000 visitors its first year; moved in 1997 for the Bricktown Canal; today at 429 Kings of Leon Lane.
- Jim Brewer Building: 101 E. California Ave, Bricktown, the building where the Haunted Warehouse began.
- "It's a great day in Bricktown" was Jim Brewer's answering-machine greeting.
- O'Brien's Bricktown Club opened March 17, 1990, with the St. Patrick's Day parade and a block party; it operated about seven years.
- Brewer Entertainment Inc. started in 1991 (per The Journal Record, 2008).

## Companies today
- [Bricktown Haunted Warehouse](https://bricktownhauntedwarehouse.com/): Oklahoma City's original haunted attraction, since 1986
- [Bricktown Event Center](https://bricktowneventcenter.com/): event venue at 425 Kings of Leon Lane
- [Bricktown Real Estate Co.](https://bricktownrealco.com/): Bricktown buildings and space for lease or sale, direct from the owner
- [BricktownTix](https://www.bricktowntix.com/): Bricktown's own ticketing platform
- [Bricktown Parking](https://bricktownparking.com/): scan-and-pay parking, no app required
- [Bricktown OKC](https://bricktownokc.com/): the Bricktown district guide
- [Yo Pablo](https://yopablonorman.com/): 21+ sports bar and grill on Campus Corner, 747 Asp Avenue, Norman
